SMTO-GWT-0091 — This work started before the Gateway's data was cleared

GUID: dc685fc1-cebe-59f3-a943-58cfb4f834ba
Slug: gateway-runtime-epoch-stale
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • This work was started before runtime data was cleared on this Gateway, so the Gateway won't accept its requests anymore. This request was refused before it ran; earlier steps of the same work may already have run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Data › Storage and make sure the runtime data purge shows completed. Work started before that cleanup belongs to the old data and can't continue on this Gateway.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. This refreshes what SMTO knows about the Gateway after the cleanup.
  3. If the earlier conversation is still there, look at its results. Also check the Gateway computer for steps that already finished, such as files written or changes made. This request didn't run, but earlier steps of the same work may have, and repeating them could do them twice. The cleanup may have removed the old conversation.
  4. Select New conversation and ask SMTO to do only the steps that did not finish. New work picks up the Gateway's current data, so the Gateway accepts it.

What success looks like

  • The new conversation runs commands on the Gateway without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and its Gateways. Don't start another runtime data purge to get past this; it won't bring the old work back.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected the request during authentication because its runtime epoch header does not match the epoch published by the Gateway's last completed runtime purge.

What this means

  • The request belongs to a Gateway runtime epoch that is no longer current. The classification describes only the condition observed by the producer.

Why this can happen

  • The request runtime epoch differs from the current Gateway generation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • The request carried a runtime_epoch that differs from the Gateway's runtime-purge epoch.json (rejected before dispatch with gateway_runtime_epoch_stale), typically because the Run was accepted before a purge. Refresh the Gateway record with Check connection and start a new Run so it captures the current epoch; reconcile any earlier uncertain operation from the old Run before repeating it.
  • Refresh the selected Gateway runtime metadata and prepare a new request. Reconcile any earlier uncertain operation before retrying it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
